Subject: Questions on operator escrow, deletion timelines under Schrems II for EU-only processing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move into procurement we need a concise technical explanation of a few controls so our legal and DPA teams can sign off on "EU-only processing" under Schrems II + SCCs. High-level asks: 

- Can you describe the operator/engineer access model for in-region inference? Specifically: are any operators able to access customer data outside a controlled workflow, and is there an escrow/attestation mechanism for operator keys?
- What is the end-to-end deletion timeline for inference artifacts (KV caches, logs, async backups) once a delete request is accepted?
- Do you provide verifiable proof of deletion or an audit snapshot we can store with the SCCs package?

We're trying to map this to our internal obligations and to the vendor risk questionnaire — I attached the vendor checklist we usually use (not included here).

Would you be able to respond in writing and also propose a 30-min slot this week for a quick technical Q&A?

Best,
Anna
Data Privacy, MediGroup GmbH
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on operator escrow, deletion timelines under Schrems II for EU-only processing

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick reply below and happy to expand on any item in a call. I also attached a short diagram and a one-page operator process summary (see attachments).

Operator access model (short):
- All in-region inference clusters run in customer-dedicated VPCs when EU-only is selected. Operator control plane access is mediated through a private control plane that authenticates and authorises via the customer's KMS-backed service account.
- Operators (Redwood engineers) can access runtime hosts only via ephemeral session brokers that issue time-limited credentials; sessions require MFA and are recorded. There is a documented escalation path and an approval workflow (2 approvals required for any session that touches logs or KV cache).
- Operator keys used for support are stored in an HSM; we can place an escrow copy for customers under an audited process. Escrow access is logged and only released with documented justification and customer notification.

Deletion and artifacts:
- KV cache: immediate invalidation on delete request; physical removal from NVMe/ephemeral memory occurs within the same maintenance window (typically <6 hours).
- Logs/traces: short-term traces for debugging are truncated and fully purged after the retention window (default 30 days, configurable). We support a 0/7/30/90 retention profile per contract.
- Backups/async snapshots: we keep a narrow rolling buffer (configurable). For EU-only customers, backups are stored in-region and are purged per the deletion policy; full removal can take up to 72 hours to ensure no replication is in-flight.

Proof of deletion / audit:
- We provide a deletion certificate (hashed artifact list + deletion timestamp + operator sign-off) and an audit log export showing the deletion actions and the operator session IDs.
- For high-assurance requests we can provide a notarised attestation from our compliance team (PDF) and a snippet of the underlying change records.

I'm copying Laura (security) and Lauren (legal) for any additions. Proposed times: Thu 09:30–10:00 CET or Fri 14:00–14:30 CET.

—Marissa
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Anna — a few legal/contract clarifications to add so procurement sees the right language: 

- Escrow: we can add a contract clause describing HSM escrow of operator keys with release conditions (court order, incident response with customer approval, etc.). We prefer an "escrow access governance" appendix that documents the approval chain rather than embedding open-ended access rights in the main SOW.
- Proofs: the deletion certificate Marissa described is the standard move; we are happy to add a clause requiring delivery of the certificate within X days of confirmed deletion (we normally commit to 5 business days).
- Residual risk: for Schrems II concerns we typically pair EU-only processing with a contractual warrant that data will not be exported except as required by law; if MediGroup needs stronger guarantees we can propose an in-region operator covenant and additional technical controls (e.g., operator access IP whitelisting to customer-managed jump hosts).

@Rishi / @Laura: anything to add on operational controls?

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Lauren — thanks for the quick answers. A few follow-ons from our security team (short list):

1) Auditability: can you produce an exportable audit package that includes operator session recordings (time-limited URLs) and the HSM access logs for any escrow release? We don't need raw recordings by default, but we need verifiable hashes and timestamps.
2) KMS separation: confirm that customer-managed KMS keys can be used for model encryption so Redwood cannot decrypt outside of customer workflows.
3) Retention profiles: we would like a tight default for in-region inference of 7 days for logs and 0 days for persisted caches, unless otherwise authorised. Can you confirm configuration and any cost delta?

If those are OK we'll draft procurement language and circulate. Also, please confirm whether the deletion certificate is machine-verifiable (signed JSON + signature) — our infra team prefers programmatic hooks.

Thanks,
Oliver
Legal & InfoSec, MediGroup GmbH

Subject: Re: Questions on operator escrow, deletion timelines under Schrems II for EU-only processing

Oliver — short answers below and a pointer to the drive pack: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/MediGroup-SCCS-Package

1) Audit package: yes — we provide an export that includes:
   - Signed manifest (hashes of deleted artifacts + timestamps)
   - Operator session IDs and corresponding session-recording reference (we provide time-limited URLs and signed hashes; recordings are retained per contract)
   - HSM access log extract (events related to escrow releases)

2) KMS separation: customers can bring their own KMS. We support envelope encryption where customer KEKs (key-encryption-keys) remain under the customer's control; Redwood never stores the unwrapped DEKs outside the enclave. That pattern is standard for our EU-only deployments.

3) Retention profiles & cost: we can set default logs to 7 days and persisted caches to 0. Operationally, setting cache=0 means we invalidate all KV cache entries immediately after session end; there is a modest latency and cost impact (approx +6–9% token cost for workloads that benefited from caching). We will provide a workload estimate once we see sample traffic.

4) Machine-verifiable deletion certificate: we will provide a signed JSON certificate (RFC-compliant signature) and an accompanying PDF attestation for legal. The JSON includes artifact hashes, deletion timestamps, operator sign-off IDs, and a Redwood signature block.

If you want, we'll prepare the exact procurement clause language and the example signed JSON for your infra team to validate. 

—Laura
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
